Implementation Plan

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends git-checkout-diag (the existing `&git-checkout-diag` YAML anchor in `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`) and the existing `tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_*.py` contract-test pattern
Scope-mode justification: The finding names one leak: the diagnostic runs `git config --list --show-origin` (line 317), which prints every config value, including `http.https://github.com/.extraheader` (an encoded `AUTHORIZATION: basic …` header). The `release` job checks out with `token: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT || github.token }}` (line ~6003) and runs the diagnostic afterwards (line 6358), so that header carries the PAT. This plan does what the recommendation asks: it removes the release job's use of the diagnostic and changes the dump so it prints key names only. That also covers the other four places the anchor runs (`resolve-version`, `e2e-smoke-test`, `validate-scripts`, `validate`), where the header carries `github.token`. Deleting the whole diagnostic is left out, because it is still marked as an open investigation into the checkout exit-128 error. The complete version, including a regression test that runs the diagnostic's own code, adds well under 30 lines over the shortcut and no new dependency or interface. The order of priorities in §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > …) favours the complete version.

## Automation / scheduler surface (§20.E)
- No new script. The change edits an existing workflow and adds one contract test.
- Where it runs: `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml` (release gate: `workflow_dispatch`, and dispatch from `auto-release-stable.yml` / `promote-main-to-stable.yml`). The new test is wired into `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `tests-release-and-log-analysis`, which runs on `pull_request` and `push`.
- No new long-running process. No database work. No entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.

## Planning ref
- Planning context: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `11eedbeb10e62fa9d5f33088a89fc917f13e3e05`, branch `claude/relaxed-johnson-nmd1pg`. The integration branch metadata names the same branch, and the mismatch flag is `false`.
- The isolated copy I read reports `e0ad06e` ("isolated snapshot") on branch `isolated`. That is the sandbox's stand-in `.git`, not a branch mismatch. Every line number below comes from that copy.

## 1. Files likely to change
- `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`
  - Lines 303–308: update the comment above `&git-checkout-diag` to say the diagnostic prints config key names only, never values, because values can include the checkout's encoded authorization header. Cite this finding.
  - Lines 316–317: replace `echo "--- config (first 200) ---"` / `git config --list --show-origin 2>&1 | head -n 200` with a keys-only form, `git config --list --name-only --show-origin 2>&1 | head -n 200`, and change the label to `--- config keys (first 200; values withheld) ---`.
  - Lines ~6355–6358, `release` job: delete the comment block and the `- *git-checkout-diag` line (four lines). This removes the diagnostic from the only job whose checkout uses `GH_PAT`.
  - Leave the anchor and its other uses (lines 309, 4388, 4698, 5975) in place. The keys-only change makes them safe. Removing the anchor itself would also mean removing every use, or YAML parsing fails.
- `tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_no_git_config_value_dump.py` (new contract test; see section 6).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `tests-release-and-log-analysis`: add a step after "Test-and-mark-stable phantom review-run filter test" (lines 1153–1156), in the same form: `name: Test-and-mark-stable git-config credential dump guard test`, run with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_no_git_config_value_dump.py`. Add it to that one job only, as `tests/test_ci_job_split_contract.py` requires.
- `changelog.d/<issue-number>-release-diagnostic-no-credential-dump.md`: a fragment starting with `<!-- changelog: security -->`, written as CLAUDE.md §20 describes.

## 2. Functions or modules to implement
- No new runtime code. The diagnostic's shell code changes on one line.
- The new test file needs these helpers:
  - `_job_block(text, job_id)`: returns the lines from `^  <job_id>:$` up to the next `^  [a-z0-9-]+:$`. Same text-slicing approach as the existing tests.
  - `_diag_run_body(text)`: returns the `run: |` body under `- &git-checkout-diag`, taken from the indented block and with the indent removed.

## 3. Data structures affected
- None.

## 4. API or interface changes
- No inputs, outputs, environment variables, step `id`s or job IDs change.
- The step name `git diagnostic (checkout exit-128 probe)` stays the same.
- Visible change in the logs: the diagnostic's config section shows `file:<origin>\t<key>` lines with no values. The release job no longer shows the diagnostic step.
- The workflow file gets slightly smaller (currently 376,566 bytes, under the 480,000-byte guard).

## Decisions

### D1 — How to stop the PAT from reaching the logs
- Chosen: keep the diagnostic, change the dump to `--name-only` so it prints keys only, and remove the diagnostic from the `release` job.
- Alternatives considered: (a) Delete the anchor and all five uses. This stops an investigation that is still open and touches more of the file. (b) Only remove the release job's use. The other jobs would still print the `github.token` header. (c) Set `persist-credentials: false` on the release checkout. Later release steps push tags with that credential, so this would break the release.
- Why: this follows both parts of the recommendation ("remove the config dump and its release-job invocation; if diagnostics remain, print configuration keys only"). It closes the leak in every job and changes the least.

### D2 — How to prevent a regression
- Chosen: a contract test that (1) fails on any `git config --list`/`-l` without `--name-only` in `.github/workflows/*.yml` or `workflow-templates/*.yml`, (2) checks the `release` job contains no `*git-checkout-diag` and no config dump, and (3) runs the diagnostic body against a scratch repo seeded with a sentinel extraheader and checks the sentinel never appears in the output.
- Alternatives considered: text checks alone, or a lint step in `static-checks`.
- Why: running the code proves the actual output contains no value, not just that a flag is present. This repo protects workflow behaviour with dedicated contract tests.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundary: secret material (`GH_PAT`, `github.token`) that `actions/checkout` stores in `.git/config` as `http.https://github.com/.extraheader`, versus the Actions logs, which anyone with read access to the logs can see. GitHub's log masking is defence in depth only. It cannot be relied on for encoded or transformed values, and it does not cover downloaded log archives that copy the text elsewhere.
- Authorization: no new endpoint or surface is added.
- Input validation: not applicable. The diagnostic reads local git state only.
- Abuse cases:
  - Someone with log access recovers the base64 `x-access-token:<PAT>` from a release-gate log and uses the PAT's `repo` + `workflow` scope across every consumer repo. Fixed: no values are printed, and the diagnostic no longer runs in the PAT-backed job.
  - A future edit brings back `git config --list` (or `-l`) in any workflow or template. The new test fails CI.
  - A remote URL with credentials embedded (`https://user:token@…`) would also have printed through `--list`. Keys-only covers that too.
- Other output already safe: the extraheader simulation in the same step already prints names only (`--get-regexp … --name-only`) and its `--unset-all` diagnostics. The copied config sits in a `mktemp` file, is cleaned up by `trap`, and is never printed. These need no change.

## 5. Risks and edge cases
- `git config --list --name-only` needs git ≥ 2.6. GitHub's ubuntu runners have far newer git. The step keeps `set +e` and `exit 0`, so it can never fail a job.
- YAML anchor/alias: removing only the release job's alias (not the anchor) keeps the file valid. The implementer must not remove the anchor (line 309) while aliases remain. Run `actionlint` / `yamllint` (CI `static-checks`) to confirm.
- The CI step must go in exactly one job (`tests/test_ci_job_split_contract.py`).
- The release gates' own `validate-scripts` job does not need to run the new test. It runs in PR/push CI.
- Logs from past runs still contain the dumped header. Removing or rotating them is outside a code change. The PR description should recommend rotating `GH_PAT` and deleting logs from past release-gate runs. This is a note for the operator, not code.
- Conflict detection: the finding cites `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:317`. That matches the current copy exactly (`git config --list --show-origin 2>&1 | head -n 200`). No conflicts found.

## 6. Testing considerations
New test `tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_no_git_config_value_dump.py`, a plain `python3` script with `test_*` functions and a `__main__` runner, like `tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_phantom_review_run_filter.py`:
1. `test_no_workflow_dumps_git_config_values`: for every `.github/workflows/*.yml` and `workflow-templates/*.yml`, flag any line matching `\bgit\s+config\b.*(--list\b|\s-l\b)` without `--name-only`.
2. `test_release_job_does_not_run_checkout_diagnostic`: `_job_block(text, "release")` contains neither `*git-checkout-diag` nor `git config --list`.
3. `test_diag_anchor_prints_keys_only`: the anchor's run body contains `--name-only` on its `--list` line.
4. `test_diag_body_does_not_leak_extraheader_value`: create a scratch repo with `git init` in a tempdir, then `git config --local http.https://github.com/.extraheader "AUTHORIZATION: basic <SENTINEL_B64>"` and `remote.origin.url https://x-access-token:<SENTINEL2>@github.com/o/r`.
